**Allowed origins**

CORS is set in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`, in the `cors({ origin: (origin) => … })` middleware. It is applied with `app.use('*', …)`. The `origin` function echoes the request origin back only if it is one of these:

- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- any origin ending in `.pages.dev`
- any origin ending in `.workers.dev`

A request with no `Origin` header gets `null`, and so does any other origin. Allowed methods are `GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS`. Allowed headers are `Content-Type` and `Authorization`. `maxAge` is 86400.

**Adding a custom domain**

Edit the `if (…)` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27` and add another `||` branch:

- For one exact domain, add `origin === 'https://play.example.com'`.
- For all subdomains, add `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`.

Don't put the domain in an array. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, so wildcards would silently fail. The code comment on line 20 and `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` both say this.

`endsWith` is loose. `.example.com` also matches `https://evil-example.com`? No, because of the leading dot. It does match any scheme or port, though, such as `http://x.example.com:9999`. If you want to be stricter, compare the full origin.

If the custom domain is on the Worker side, you don't need to change CORS. A Worker route or custom domain in `worker/wrangler.toml` only changes where the API is served. CORS depends only on the origin of the frontend page.

I didn't check the frontend's API base URL setting. If the frontend moves to the new domain, that URL may need updating too. I also haven't read `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4, which the docs link to for CORS.
